subject: Multi-region Dedicated: packaging, throughput guarantees & cross-region DR
messages:
From: Claire Reynolds <claire.reynolds@acme-ops.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exploring multi-region Dedicated + DR options

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a multi-region inference footprint (primary US, DR EU) and have a few questions before we finalize procurement:

- Do you price Dedicated as separate GPU pools per region, or can we purchase a single committed pool with cross-region routing?
- For replication/DR, what are the options and typical incremental costs (active-active vs. hot-standby)?
- How do throughput guarantees work for bursty workloads across regions? Can committed capacity be reserved for cross-region failover?

We're targeting ~64 A100-equivalent GPUs in US (steady) and a smaller hot-standby in EU (16 GPUs) with the ability to failover within 60s. Procurement will need a clear statement of work and an estimate for a 12-month reserved commit.

Can you share a packaging option and a ballpark monthly cost including any replication overhead? Also include any early-commit discount thresholds.

Thanks,
Claire
Head of AI Ops, Acme Operations

[Attachment: acme-requirements-brief.pdf]

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Reynolds <claire.reynolds@acme-ops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-region Dedicated + DR options

Claire — great questions. High-level answers and a couple of packaging sketches below. Sharing internally for pricing confirmation, looped Marissa for discounts and SOW.

1) Pool topology options
- Separate regional pools (recommended for strict data residency): two distinct commits, billed per-region. Easier SLAs and capacity isolation.
- Single global commit with routing: we can route by policy but this requires cross-region replication of model artifacts and a global orchestration layer; typically adds 8–12% overhead to unit costs and some limits on strict residency.

2) DR/replication patterns
- Hot-standby (standby pool sized at ~25% of primary): lower steady cost; failover within 60–90s with warmed KV caches and prefix caching.
- Active-active (mirrored capacity): higher cost (~100% of primary) but warm response times and sub-5s failover. Cross-region replication adds network egress and syncing costs — we typically estimate ~6–10% of committed spend for continuous replication depending on model checkpoint sizes and frequency.

3) Throughput & guarantees
- Commit tiers provide SLO-backed throughput windows (tokens/sec / GPU). For bursty windows we recommend configuring burst capacity (uncommitted pool) or autoscale buffers. We can guarantee baseline p95 latency for committed throughput; bursts are best-effort unless you add burst reservation.

Preliminary numbers (ballpark, monthly):
- Option A (separate pools, US 64 GPUs committed + EU 16 GPU hot-standby): $165,000 / month committed + estimated replication/standby overhead $9,000 / month => ~$174k/mo.
- Option B (global commit with cross-region routing, equivalent capacity): $170,000 / month + routing/replication overhead (~$12k) => ~$182k/mo (includes 8% routing overhead).

Discounts: 15% at 12-month commit baseline for this deal size; we can consider 18–20% with an earlier signature or an expanded commit (e.g., commit to 80 GPUs total). Marissa, can you confirm final discounting and whether we can offer additional credits for onboarding?

I attached a short pricing sketch (redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf) and a draft SOW. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the trade-offs.

— Logan
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf, SOW-acme-dedicated-draft.docx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Claire Reynolds <claire.reynolds@acme-ops.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-region Dedicated + DR options

Claire — thanks for the level-setting. A few commercial clarifications and a proposed concession: 

- We can offer a multi-region package with per-region isolation but a single contract and consolidated billing. That keeps data-residency per-region while simplifying procurement.
- For the numbers Logan posted, I can confirm: 15% standard for 12-mo at these sizes. We can extend to 20% if Acme signs within 14 days and commits to a minimum 80-GPU total (US primary + EU standby scaled slightly to 20).
- On failover credits: we can include a one-time failover readiness exercise (runbook, DR test) and one DR test/year at no extra charge. Ongoing replication egress is billed separately as Logan noted.

Marissa (I lead enterprise deals for Dedicated).

Action items:
1) Claire to confirm whether you need strict per-region enforcement (separate pools) or consolidated contract with region isolation.
2) If Acme agrees to 80-GPU 12-mo commit and signs within 2 weeks, we will offer 20% off list and $40k onboarding credit (applied in month 1).

— Marissa
VP, Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Reynolds <claire.reynolds@acme-ops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@legalpartner.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:54:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-region Dedicated + DR options

Thanks Logan/Marissa — helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/legal: 

- On the consolidated contract with per-region isolation: that works better for our purchasing team as long as SLA and data-residency are explicit in the SOW.
- For active-active vs hot-standby: our app tolerates short failovers but we need less than 60s RTO for the main inference path. Hot-standby sized at 25% might be risky. Can we propose hot-standby at 33% and a formal DR runbook included in the SOW?
- Regarding discounting: the 20% + $40k onboarding credit is attractive. One ask — can we structure a 12-month commit with a 6-month re-evaluation window to optionally reallocate up to 10% of committed GPUs between regions without penalty? This helps us manage seasonality.

Samir: looping you for legal on the reallocation allowance and the SLA language.

Claire

On Thu, Jun 10, 2026 at 11:03 AM Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Claire — great questions. High-level answers and a couple of packaging sketches below....

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Claire Reynolds <claire.reynolds@acme-ops.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exploring multi-region Dedicated + DR options

Claire — we can accommodate the asks. Final commercial position below so you have something to take to procurement: 

- Commitment: 80 GPUs total (US: 60 committed, EU: 20 standby).
- Hot-standby sizing: we'll set EU standby at 33% of primary performance equivalent (20 GPUs) as requested.
- Flexibility: a 6-month re-evaluation clause allowing one-time reallocation of up to 10% of committed GPUs between regions with 30 days notice; reallocation will re-balance billing pro rata for the remainder of the term.
- SLA & DR: full SLO language and DR runbook will be included in the SOW; DR test included once per 12-month term.
- Price: list $185,000/mo; 20% discount applied => $148,000/mo. Onboarding credit: $40,000 in month 1. Replication/egress estimated at $11,500/mo (separate line item).

Next steps:
1) I'll send updated SOW and a DocuSign for signature by EOD 2026-06-13 if you confirm.
2) Logan/Stephanie will schedule a 45-minute DR runbook walk-through and a technical readiness call.

If that sounds good Claire, we can lock the concession for two weeks.

— Marissa
VP, Sales — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
